related_questions.snippet: The ICD-10 code for a routine complete blood count (CBC) screening is Z13. 0: Encounter for screening for diseases of the blood and blood-forming organs. This code is used when the CBC is performed as a preventive measure rather than for diagnosing a specific condition.

related_questions.question: What is the ICD-10 code for CBC unspecified?

text_blocks.snippet: The ICD-10 code for an unspecified complete blood count (CBC) is R79.9 for abnormal findings of blood chemistry, unspecified. If the CBC reveals a specific abnormality, like decreased white blood cell count, the code would be more specific (e.g., D72.819 for decreased white blood cell count, unspecified). If the CBC is part of a screening, Z13.0 (encounter for screening for diseases of the blood and blood-forming organs) may be appropriate.

list.title: R79.9:
list.snippet: This code is used when the blood test results are abnormal, but the specific abnormality is not documented or specified.

list.title: D72.819:
list.snippet: This code is used if the CBC shows a decreased white blood cell count that is not otherwise specified.

list.title: Z13.0:
list.snippet: This code is used when a CBC is performed as part of a routine health check or screening.

list.title: Other Specific Codes:
list.snippet: If the CBC reveals a specific abnormality like anemia, neutropenia, or elevated white blood cell count, there are more specific codes available within the D64.9 (Anemia, unspecified), D70.9 (Neutropenia, unspecified), D72.829 (Elevated white blood cell count, unspecified), etc.

related_questions.question: What diagnosis can be used for a CBC?
related_questions.snippet: It can detect blood cancers, anemia, infections and other conditions. For a CBC blood test, a healthcare provider takes a sample of your blood and sends it to a lab. The lab measures the amount of red blood cells, hemoglobin (the protein that carries oxygen in your red blood cells), white blood cells and platelets.

text_blocks.snippet: This code is used when a CBC is performed as a routine screening test, without a specific diagnosis in mind.
If an abnormal CBC result is found, the appropriate diagnosis code for the specific abnormality should be used. For example, if anemia is detected, the code D64.9 (Anemia, unspecified) may be used.
